medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The School of Medicine, in a culture of community, scholarship, and innovation, is dedicated to inspiring diverse and promising students to lead and transform medicine for the betterment of humanity. Crucial to this effort is developing a student body with many perspectives and backgrounds and creating a welcoming campus climate. The Office of Engagement & Excellence works closely with Admissions, Student Affairs, Student Council, and the Hofstra and Northwell communities to provide broad experiences to all students, including two student leadership positions within Student Council -the Co-Chair for New & Prospective Students and Diversity Night Chair. Diversity Night is an annual event which celebrates the various cultures, traditions, and expressions represented at the School of Medicine. Medical Students can also participate in Healthy Living Long Island and NextGen Healers, two public health initiatives designed to teach elementary school students in a local underserved community.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence:
Students enrolled in the Hofstra Northwell School of Medicine ("School of Medicine") can apply for a one year Leave of Absence (LOA) for academic or personal reasons. Students considering a LOA should speak with the Associate Dean for Student Affairs. If it is determined that the student would like to move forward with a LOA, a LOA Request Form must be completed under the guidance of the Associate Dean for Student Affairs. The form must include the reasons for the leave and the anticipated date of return. Students are required to meet with the departments listed on the LOA Form to discuss any implications that could result from the absence. Students will receive a written decision from the Associate Dean for Student Affairs within two weeks of the meeting, which also may include conditions for the granting of a leave. The Associate Dean for Student Affairs will also notify additional offices within the School of Medicine of the student's status, as needed.

medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Student life at the Zucker School of Medicine is enriched through extracurricular activities. Over 80 active student organizations provide opportunities to support students’ professional growth and personal development. These include opportunities to expand their leadership by chairing major events and representing peers through the Student Council. Students invest in their communities through service projects, health outreach, and mentorship programs. They support one another through wellness programming, social events, and creative outlets that are restorative during the demands of medical training and invest in their futures through research, symposiums, specialty panels, and professional development events. In 2025-26, students organized over 166 events, reflecting a school culture that understands great physicians are shaped not only through patient and classroom experiences, but also through activities that support professional and personal development.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: Once the training facility of the New York Jets professional football team, the renovated Medical Education Center is now the home for the Donald and Barbara Zucker School of Medicine at Hofstra/Northwell. Our location, 25 miles from Manhattan, affords students a suburban setting while being close to the excitement of the city, which is easily accessible by car or Long Island Rail Road. The University runs frequent shuttles to nearby train stations, local restaurants and shopping malls. The School of Medicine's location puts students in close proximity to Jones Beach and Long Beach, parks, golf courses and sporting arenas. The famed resort area, the Hamptons on Long Island's East End, is a little more than an hour's drive away.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Housing options for medical students vary based on personal preference, with the majority choosing to live off campus. Many students value the flexibility, independence, and cost-effectiveness of securing their own apartments or shared housing in the surrounding community. Students are responsible for arranging their off-campus housing; however, current medical students provide support through an open housing list managed by Student Council and are available to offer guidance and share insights about neighborhoods and rental options. For those seeking a university-managed option, students may apply for a space in the Graduate Residence Hall, Hofstra University’s newest residential facility. This five-story building features apartment- and suite-style units with kitchenettes, shared common spaces, on-site laundry and one-and-a-half bathrooms. The residence hall is conveniently located within walking distance of the School of Medicine.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: OUTMed is the school's LGBT+ and Allies organization. It serves as a space for those who identify as LGBT+ and those who identify as allies to foster discussions on LGBT issues. The American Medical Women's Association (AMWA) is an organization of physicians, medical students, allies, and other persons dedicated to serving as the unique voice for women's health and the advancement of women in medicine. Events are held throughout the year by the local chapter to foster relationships. Both organizations are open to all.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: The Offices of Academic Success and Student Affairs support applicants and learners with temporary and chronic disabilities by facilitating equal access to the educational program and promoting well-being. In addition to an ADA-aligned accommodations request and implementation process, we partner with Hofstra University’s Student Access Services office to secure resources to support accommodations. The Zucker School of Medicine maintains a student health insurance plan for purchase, helps connect students with local healthcare providers, and protects time for regular healthcare appointments through the Policy on Access to Healthcare Services. The ZSOM Medical Student Well-Being program promotes resources for intellectual, emotional, and social well-being. Mental Health services include Hofstra University’s Counseling Center, Northwell Health’s Behavioral Health College Partnership and Physician Resource Network, and telehealth through TimelyCare.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
The Office of Student Affairs supports the continued development of the whole person during medical school through the Medical Student Well-Being program, which focuses on resources specific to the seven dimensions of well-being: emotional, intellectual, financial, occupational, social, spiritual and physical.

Addressing mental health concerns and receiving care for behavioral health is crucial to supporting medical student well-being. Medical students have access to several different options for referrals for behavioral healthcare. Tips for Cognitive Endurance, hosted by the Office of Student Affairs in partnership with Northwell Health's Behavioral Health College Partnership, are informal monthly sessions to proactively address well-being and build cognitive endurance during medical school. Well-being stretches across several aspects of an individual’s life and the medical school has resources available to students, such as career advisement, student finance, academic success, engagement and excellence, student records and more. Students are encouraged to explore faith & spirituality through the Prayer & Reflection space in the Student Lounge, Hofstra's Interfaith Center and Northwell's Chaplaincy Services. Student Council and the 80+ student organizations host events that encompass every dimension of medical student wellbeing. Whether it be joining the running club for a race or taking part in the Pride Parade with OutMed, there are endless opportunities for meaningful engagement. Physical wellbeing is supported by access to Hofstra's Fitness Center to take a class or walk the track, utilizing the Pride Pantry to address food insecurity, or browsing the ZSOM Outdoor Guide for local trails.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
The Donald and Barbara Zucker School of Medicine at Hofstra/Northwell fosters an inclusive campus culture focused on community, scholarship, and innovation. With around 100 students per class, ZSOM is a place where students, faculty, and staff know one another by name and the school promotes a close-knit environment for collaboration and relationship-building. 
 
Student life is enhanced by over 80 active organizations, including the Student Council, which organizes events and represents student interests. These organizations offer opportunities for leadership, community service, professional, and personal growth, allowing students to customize their experiences aligned with their interests alongside their academic commitments.
 
The Zucker School of Medicine offers a dynamic, supportive culture that combines rigorous academics with a strong community and extracurricular opportunities, preparing students to become passionate, innovative leaders in medicine.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo:
All Zucker School of Medicine students are responsible for transportation to and from all learning sites. The school is not responsible for transporting students, and out of fairness to all students, will not make site assignments or curricular adjustments for individual students based on transportation preferences.

Public transportation is limited. All students are required to have a valid driver’s license and access to a car, with possible exceptions for students with recognized disabilities.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Student study spaces are intentionally near faculty offices for support. Faculty offer office hours and review sessions. Our Office of Academic Success has dedicated faculty and runs peer tutoring.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students see patients beginning week 1 in our EMT curriculum. Subsequently, they have a weekly half day in Medicine, Pediatric, Ob/Gyn, Surgery and Psychiatry practices throughout the first two years.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: In person, hands-on, experiential; become EMTs, immersed in offices learning from patients. Self-directed, flipped classroom, large/small group interactive sessions, hybrid problem/case-based.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Students complete clerkships during 3rd year at our Northwell hospitals in Medicine, Pediatrics, Surgery, Ob/Gyn, Neurology and Psychiatry. During 4th year, students complete three Acting Internships.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Yes, attendance is expected at all sessions. Sessions take place in-person.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
Experiential learning is at the core of our educational program. Beginning on day one of medical school, Zucker School of Medicine at Hofstra/Northwell students start their clinical experiences by training to become Emergency Medical Technicians (EMTs) and work on Northwell Health ambulances, developing skills to establish rapport with patients, and learning to take a complete history and perform a physical examination, including performing point of care ultrasound. At the same time, students work in teams to learn critical thinking and basic sciences through clinical cases in our case/problem-based learning program, PEARLS (Patient-centered Explorations in Active Reasoning, Learning and Synthesis). By week nine of medical school, students begin to collaborate one-on-one with physicians and, before even starting third-year clerkships, will have accrued close to 200 hours taking histories and performing physical examinations with patients in medicine, OB/GYN, surgery, pediatric, and psychiatry practices.

Our culture emphasizes learning over teaching. Students are self-directed learners who hone their research, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills. Collaboration is vital in healthcare and achieving the best patient outcomes. Each week, during PEARLS, students work in small teams on clinical cases to learn the basic sciences and develop critical thinking skills. In-person attendance is essential for fostering connections and group learning. Students work closely with peers, faculty, and staff and have opportunities for co-creating learning, mentorship, and professional identity formation. Our graduating students consistently rate our program among the top in the country for integrating basic and clinical sciences and providing an exceptional learning environment. At the Zucker School of Medicine,  students learn to transform knowledge into impactful action!
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: The educational program of the Zucker School of Medicine at Hofstra/Northwell is not focused solely upon primary care. Our goal is to graduate students who are interested and excited to start a career in any discipline of medicine, including primary care.  We provide our graduates with exposure to all specialties of medicine and the skill set to excel wherever their interests and passions lead them. For interested students, our IMPACcT (Improving Patient Access, Care, and cost through Training) program offers a mentored primary care experience that integrates education and clinical skills focused on patient-centered care, quality improvement, and population health in an interprofessional, team-based setting.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: The School of Medicine recognizes the importance of research and encourages students to explore opportunities in their respective fields of study. Students may choose from several types of research projects that explore a variety of key areas in medicine, including studies in basic science, clinical research, community health, medical education, medical humanities, and quality improvement. Over 95% of students engage in research. The Office of Medical Student Research helps students connect with mentors to engage in research with scientists and physicians from the Feinstein Institutes of Medicine, Northwell Health, and Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory. For an extensive research experience, students may apply to our MD/PhD program. A one-year Master’s program in biomedical research, open to all MD students, is also offered. Each year 3rd and 4th year students apply for Graduation with Distinction in Research which recognizes those who have made significant progress in a research project.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: The Community Service Committee is one of the most active student extracurricular activities at the Zucker School of Medicine.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Northwell Health is one of the largest health systems in the US. As a partner of the Zucker School of Medicine, it sponsors 180+ ACGME training programs and educates over 1900 house staff.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Grading during years 1 &2 – Pass/Fail, Grading during clerkships and Acting Internships: Honors, High Pass, Pass, Fail

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The Zucker School of Medicine at Hofstra/Northwell is gaining recognition as a leader in medical education, drawing on Hofstra University’s academic resources and Northwell Health’s clinical facilities and research opportunities. We graduate physicians who earn the trust of their patients and the respect of their colleagues with a scientifically anchored and team-based approach to patient care. Students gain exposure to various clinical settings, including Northwell’s Center for Learning Innovation, preparing them for healthcare delivery. We cultivate critical inquiry and life-long learning, empowering students to examine factors influencing patient health to provide comprehensive and compassionate care. Zucker School of Medicine graduates achieve outstanding residency placements, reflecting our commitment to excellence in medical education. Our focus on research and innovation equips graduates to excel in a rapidly evolving healthcare landscape and positively impact patient outcomes.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
The School of Medicine, in a culture of community, scholarship, and innovation, is dedicated to inspiring diverse and promising students to lead and transform medicine for the betterment of humanity. 

The School of Medicine aims to establish itself as a revered institution of higher medical education by means of accomplishing the following visionary objectives:
To be a premier "Millennial Medical School"
To be a major contributor to the redefining of medical education
To have positively changed the University, Northwell Health and the community
To have improved the health of the region
medSchoolInformation.programAbout:
Entry to this program is highly selective, and only those who demonstrate superior high school achievement and academic aptitude, and who apply to Hofstra as first-time, full-time freshmen will be considered. International students are not eligible for this program.

BS-BA/MD Dual Degree Program students will have highly skilled advisement specialists to help determine the best choice of major for their interests and aspirations. Dual-degree candidates will also participate in the Stuart and Nancy Rabinowitz Honors College, pursue a minor in a secondary area of study, study abroad, or any combination of the three.

medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: If your school does not have a Premedical Committee, or a considerable amount of time has passed since graduation, you may submit three individual letters of recommendation – two letters from individual professors (at least one in science), and one letter from a non-academic professional (included with AMCAS application). Applicants may submit more than three letters of recommendation through AMCAS, though we do not guarantee that all letters beyond the minimum requirement will be read.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: The interview day is organized to introduce prospective students to the many exciting opportunities available at the Zucker School of Medicine at Hofstra/Northwell. By the day's end, our hope is that through meeting and interacting with faculty, students and administrators, applicants gain a comprehensive understanding of what it is like to be a student at the School of Medicine.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: Interviews will be conducted virtually for the 2025-2026 cycle in the MMI format.
medSchoolApplication.edpAvailableTxt: All application materials, including a completed AMCAS application, and all secondary materials must be received by August 1. Final admissions decisions will be sent by September 1.

The Donald and Barbara Zucker School of Medicine at Hofstra/Northwell (ZSOM) follows the Application and Acceptance Protocols and utilizes the Choose Your Medical School Tool established by the AAMC. Additional school-specific procedures are listed below. 

February 19: "Plan to Enroll"* option becomes available for accepted applicants in AMCAS through the "Choose Your Medical School Tool" 

April 15: Accepted applicants must narrow their school selections down to three, as per AAMC acceptance protocols 

April 30:
 - National Decision Deadline; if ZSOM is the first choice for an accepted applicant, they must select Plan to Enroll 
-"Commit to Enroll" ** option becomes available in AMCAS, through the "Choose your Medical School Tool" for accepted applicants who are ready to commit and withdraw all other applications (including waitlists). 

July 1: Accepted applicants must select Commit to Enroll 

Appendix: 
*Plan to Enroll: On February 19, accepted applicants can begin to select “Plan to Enroll” for their top medical school choice in the AMCAS Choose Your Medical School Tool. Applicants may hold waitlist positions at other schools and can continue to hold multiple acceptances until April 30. We ask that you choose this action as early as possible if our school is your top choice. 
**Commit to Enroll: On April 30, accepted applicants can begin to select “Commit to Enroll” when they are ready to make their final selection in the AMCAS Choose Your Medical School Tool. This indicates that you have withdrawn all other applications, including waitlist positions from other schools, and that you are committed to one final acceptance.

medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo:
All medical students must meet our academic, professionalism, and technical standards to matriculate, progress through the curriculum, and meet the requirements for graduation from the Zucker School of Medicine.

Medical education requires that the accumulation of scientific knowledge be accompanied by the simultaneous development of specific skills and competencies. Without the capability to meet our technical standards, students cannot fulfill the requirements of all the courses and clerkships at the Zucker School of Medicine. 

The Zucker School of Medicine is committed to providing qualified students with reasonable accommodations in accordance with applicable law so that they may complete their course of study and clinical experiences.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
The Office of Student Finance at the School of Medicine supports applicants and students throughout the financial aid application process and beyond. All accepted applicants are eligible to apply for financial assistance. Available funding includes federal, institutional, and private loans, as well as tuition scholarships awarded based on a combination of merit and financial need.

Students with special circumstances may submit a financial aid appeal each year for consideration of potential adjustments to their aid packages. The School of Medicine also offers a Student Emergency Fund, which allows students who have maximized their standard aid eligibility and are experiencing emergency financial needs to apply for up to $500 in additional assistance.

The Office of Student Finance is available to discuss all aspects of financial planning for medical school, including the application process, award packages, budgeting, and borrowing strategies. The Office also provides a comprehensive financial literacy program designed to help students manage their finances during medical school and prepare for residency.

medSchoolPrograms.info: Students are eligible to apply for admission to the MD/MPH, MD/MBA, MD/MA, or MD/MS programs post matriculation. The goal of the joint degree program is to facilitate the attainment of both degrees within five years. Accepted students take an additional year between their third and final (fifth) year of training to complete the majority of their MPH, MBA, MA, or MS course work. Most MD/MPH, MD/MBA, MD/MA, and MD/MS students use a portion of their elective time during their final year of medical school to complete MBA, MPH, or MA course work.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
The School of Medicine (SOM) believes that the study of medicine is enriched by contact with other intellectual disciplines; therefore, it seeks students with a diverse blend of educational backgrounds. A background in liberal arts courses that have required a student to read broadly, write extensively, and present oral arguments on topics such as history, literature, philosophy, religion, political science, anthropology, psychology, and/or sociology is highly recommended.

While it does not require a specific set of undergraduate courses in the natural sciences, the SOM recommends that candidates complete the following:
One year of college Biology with Lab
Chemistry, to the level of organic or biochemistry
One year of college Mathematics, preferably including Statistics
One year of college Physics
English Literature or Equivalent, including Writing
Additional coursework in embryology, cell biology, ethics, molecular biology and genetics is recommended, but not required, for admission.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
Selection criteria include academic credentials; personal traits; including character; motivation; capacity for work experiences in the health sciences or community; career objectives; and the individual's ability to make a positive contribution to society, the profession, and the SOM.

Specifically, the Admissions Committee considers, among others: personal statement describing personal, educational and social backgrounds; response to personal challenges; character traits including honesty, integrity, leadership, team work, empathy, maturity, emotional stability, creativity and self-direction; ability to communicate; perseverance through adversity; academic performance and GPA; rigor of undergraduate study, honors and awards, MCAT scores; extracurricular activities including community service, leadership and unique accomplishments; capacity to contribute diversity to the educational environment; employment and research experience; and a commitment to a future career in medicine.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Shadowing is viewed by the School of Medicine as a good introduction to the medical profession. We prefer our applicants to engage in hands on experiences as our curriculum centers around science in action.
